questions.prompt: What did the micro-break review find about overall performance?
questions.answer: The pooled overall performance effect was not statistically significant, despite small average benefits for fatigue and vigour.
questions.feedback: Avoid translating well-being benefits into guaranteed output gains.

questions.prompt: Can breaks substitute for adequate sleep?
questions.feedback: Distinguish short-term relief from sleep opportunity.

questions.prompt: Why might a rising error rate not prove fatigue?
questions.answer: Task difficulty, practice order and other factors may differ.

questions.prompt: What should persistent or impairing fatigue prompt?
questions.answer: Review workload and health context and seek appropriate professional advice if needed.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Justifies a recovery choice using quality and safety, recognises competing explanations and appropriate referral.
scoring.transfer: Submit a fictional attention audit covering demands, interruption triage, two protected-session designs and a recovery decision. Include output measures and one condition requiring professional or organisational support. Repeat the audit on a novel case after a delay.
scoring.pass: All four mapped course criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety boundaries. Quiz score alone cannot certify competency.
